{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社|qid=Q22119059}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|ceb|Minamisaku-gun|de|Minamisaku-gun|fi|Minami-Sakun piirikunta|fr|District de Minamisaku|id|Distrik Minamisaku, Nagano|it|Distretto di Minamisaku|ja|南佐久郡|ko|미나미사쿠군|pl|Powiat Minamisaku|uk|Повіт Мінамі-Саку|zh|南佐久郡|qid=Q1154776}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|ceb|Kitasaku-gun|de|Kitasaku-gun|fi|Kita-Sakun piirikunta|fr|District de Kitasaku|it|Distretto di Kitasaku|ja|北佐久郡|ko|기타사쿠군|pl|Powiat Kitasaku|uk|Повіт Кіта-Саку|zh|北佐久郡|qid=Q1142451}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|ceb|Chiisakata-gun|de|Chiisagata-gun|fa|منطقه چیساگاتا، ناگانو|fi|Chiisagatan piirikunta|fr|District de Chiisagata|it|Distretto di Chiisagata|ja|小県郡|ko|지사가타군|pl|Powiat Chiisagata|uk|Повіт Тіїсаґата|vi|Chiisagata, Nagano|zh|小縣郡|qid=Q1072595|lt=Chiisagata District, Nagano}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Taguchi|ja|田口村 (長野県)|ko|다구치촌 (나가노현)|qid=Q17175714}}, {{ill|Saku, Nagano|ar|ساكو (ناغانو)|azb|ساکو، ناقانو|be|Саку (горад)|ce|Саку (гӀала)|ceb|Saku (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Saku (Nagano)|de|Saku (Nagano)|eo|Saku|es|Saku (Nagano)|et|Saku (Jaapan)|fa|ساکو، ناگانو|fi|Saku (Nagano)|fr|Saku (Japon)|gl|Saku|hy|Սակու (քաղաք)|id|Saku, Nagano|it|Saku (Giappone)|ja|佐久市|ko|사쿠시|mzn|ساکو، ناگانو|nl|Saku (Nagano)|pl|Saku (miasto)|pt|Saku (Nagano)|ro|Saku|ru|Саку (город)|sh|Saku|sr|Саку (Јапан)|sv|Saku, Nagano|tg|Саку|th|ซากุ|tl|Saku, Nagano|tr|Saku, Nagano|tt|Саку (шәһәр)|uk|Саку (Наґано)|ur|ساکو، ناگانو|vi|Saku, Nagano|war|Saku, Nagano|zh|佐久市|zh_classical|佐久市|zh_min_nan|Saku-chhī|zh_yue|佐久|qid=Q495821|lt=Saku, Nagano}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|Saku District, Shinano|fa|ناحیه ساکو، شینانو|ff|Saku District, Shinano|ja|佐久郡|qid=Q7403130|lt=Saku District}} . The {{ill|Saijin|en|Saijin|lt=Enshrined deities}} are {{ill|Okihagi no Mikoto|en|Okihagi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Homudawake no Mikoto}} . {{ill|Mon (emblem)|ar|كامون|az|Kamon|be|Камон|ca|Mon (emblema)|cs|Mon (znak)|da|Mon|de|Mon (Japan)|eo|Mon (heraldiko)|es|Kamon|et|Kamon|eu|Kamon|fa|مون|fi|Mon (tunnus)|fr|Mon (héraldique)|fy|Mon (embleem)|gl|Kamon|he|מון (כתר)|hr|Mon|id|Mon (lambang)|it|Mon (emblema)|ja|家紋|kk|Камон|ko|가몬|lv|Japānas heraldika|ms|Mon (lambang)|nl|Mon (heraldiek)|no|Mon (symbol)|pl|Kamon (symbol)|pt|Mon (símbolo)|ru|Камон|sv|Mon (symbol)|tr|Mon (simge)|uk|Мон (емблема)|vi|Mon (biểu tượng)|zh|家紋|qid=Q600964|lt=The sacred crest}} is {{ill|the Kaji leaf|en|the Kaji leaf}} . The founding date is unknown.

== Overview ==
The main enshrined deity, {{ill|Okihagi|en|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto}}, is the grandson of the Great God {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|abstract|Q696362|ar|إزومو-تايشا|cs|Svatyně Izumo|de|Izumo-Taisha|es|Izumo Taisha|eu|Izumo-taisha|fi|Izumo-taisha|fr|Izumo-taisha|gl|Izumo Taisha|he|איזומו טאיישה|hu|Izumo-taisa|id|Izumo Taisha|it|Santuario di Izumo|ja|出雲大社|jv|Izumo Taisha|ka|იძუმო-ტაიშა|ko|이즈모 대사|la|Izumo-taisha|mk|Изумо-тајша|or|ଇଜୁମୋ ତାଇଶା|pl|Izumo-taisha|pt|Santuário de Izumo|ro|Marele Sanctuar de la Izumo|ru|Идзумо тайся|simple|Izumo-taisha|th|ศาลเจ้าอิซูโมะ|tr|Izumo-taisha|uk|Святилище Ідзумо|wuu|出云大社|zh|出雲大社|qid=Q696362|lt=Izumo Taisha}} and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}} from {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa taisha}}, and his mother is {{ill|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami}} ({{ill|Arafune Daimyojin|en|Arafune Daimyojin}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the {{ill|Kofun period|af|Kofun-tydperk|ar|فترة كوفون|az|Kofun dövrü|be|Кафун|bg|Кофун|bn|কোফুন যুগ|ca|Període Kofun|cs|Období Kofun|de|Kofun-Zeit|eo|Kofun-epoko|es|Período Kofun|eu|Kofun aroa|fa|دوره کوفون|fi|Kofun-kausi|fr|Période Kofun|he|תקופת קופון|hr|Razdoblje Kofun|hu|Kofun-kor|id|Zaman Kofun|it|Periodo Kofun|ja|古墳時代|ko|고훈 시대|lt|Kofun laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Kofun|nl|Kofunperiode|pl|Kofun (okres)|pt|Período Kofun|ro|Perioada Kofun|ru|Период Кофун|sh|Kofunski period|simple|Kofun period|sk|Obdobie Kofun|sl|Obdobje Kofun|sr|Кофун период|sv|Kofunperioden|th|ยุคโคฟุง|tl|Panahong Kofun|tr|Kofun Dönemi|uk|Період Кофун|vi|Thời kỳ Kofun|wuu|古坟时代|zh|古坟时代|zh_min_nan|Kohun sî-tāi|zh_yue|古墳時代|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba}}" from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ar|فترة نانبوكو تشو|bg|Нанбоку-чо|bn|নান্‌বোকু-চোও যুগ|ca|Període Nanboku-chō|cs|Období Nanbokučó|de|Namboku-chō|es|Período Nanbokuchō|eu|Nanboku-chō Aroa|fa|دوره نانبوکوچو|fi|Nanboku-chō-kausi|fr|Époque Nanboku-chō|he|תקופת שתי החצרות הקיסריות|hu|A japán császári udvar különválása|id|Zaman Nanboku-chō|it|Periodo Nanboku-chō|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|ko|남북조 시대 (일본)|ms|Tempoh Nanboku-chō|nl|Nanboku-cho-periode|pt|Período Nanboku-chō|ru|Период Намбокутё|simple|Nanboku-chō period|sr|Нанбокућо период|sv|Nanboku-chō|th|ยุคราชสำนักเหนือ-ใต้|tr|Nanboku-chō Dönemi|uk|Період Намбокутьо|vi|Nam–Bắc triều (Nhật Bản)|zh|南北朝时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Nanboku-tyô sî-tāi|zh_yue|南北朝 (日本)|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}} introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."

During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>

== Cultural Assets ==

=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===

* Three-storied pagodas - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref>
* East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto

== Shrine precincts ==

* {{ill|Kinugasa Shrine|en|Kinugasa Shrine}}
* {{ill|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en|Fukuda Inari Shrine}}

In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>

== Sacred Tree ==
[[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]]
There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|Cryptomeria|ar|سرو اليابان|arz|سرو اليابان|az|Yapon kriptomeriyası|ca|Criptomèria|ceb|Cryptomeria japonica|cs|Kryptomerie japonská|da|Japansk kryptomeria|de|Sicheltanne|dsb|Japańska kryptomerija|el|Ιαπωνικό κυπαρίσσι|eo|Sugio|es|Cryptomeria japonica|et|Jaapani krüptomeeria|eu|Japoniar zedro|fa|سدر ژاپنی|fi|Sugi|fr|Cryptomeria japonica|frr|Cryptomeria japonica|ga|Céadar Seapánach|gl|Criptomeria|he|קריפטומריה|hr|Japanska kriptomerija|hsb|Japanska kryptomerija|hu|Japánciprus|hy|Կրիպտոմերիա ճապոնական|id|Cryptomeria|is|Keisaraviður|it|Cryptomeria japonica|ja|スギ|ka|იაპონური კრიპტომერია|kn|ಕ್ರಿಪ್ಟೋಮೀರಿಯ|ko|삼나무|koi|Криптомерия|kv|Криптомерия|lt|Japoninė kriptomerija|mrj|Криптомери|ne|धुपी सल्ला|nl|Sikkelcipres|no|Japanseder|pl|Kryptomeria japońska|pms|Cryptomeria japonica|pt|Cryptomeria japonica|ro|Criptomeria|ru|Криптомерия|sl|Japonska kriptomerija|su|Cedar Jepang|sv|Kryptomeria|tr|Japon çamı|udm|Криптомерия|uk|Криптомерія японська|vi|Liễu sam|war|Cryptomeria japonica|zh|日本柳杉|qid=Q147388|lt=Cryptomeria}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|Nio (Buddhism)|ar|نيو|ca|Niō|cs|Nió|eo|Nioo|es|Niō|eu|Nio|fr|Niō|hu|Nio|id|Niō|it|Nio (buddismo)|ja|金剛力士|ko|금강역사|pl|Niō|pt|Nio (budismo)|ro|Niō|ru|Конго рикиси|th|นิโอ|zh|金剛力士|qid=Q539715|lt=the Niomon Gate}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|Honda Seiroku|de|Honda Seiroku|ja|本多静六|qid=Q11520098}}, a doctor of {{ill|Doctor of Philosophy in Forestry|ja|博士（林学）|qid=Q98117672}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />

== Anecdote ==

* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|gokou|ja|御幸|qid=Q16280183}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> .
* Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref>
* {{ill|Mayor of Saku City|en|Mayor of Saku City}}, {{ill|Seiji Yanagida|ja|柳田清二|qid=Q17222140}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>
